blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 3

Charles Darwin, the brilliant anthropologist and creator of the theory of evolution, is not normally associated with the modern business world. Nevertheless, Darwinian evolutionary theory is the foundation of a new wave of ideas about human behaviour in general and particularly the way people behave in the workplace; these ideas have given the title of 'evolutionary psychology'. Evolutionary psychology revolves around the notion that our brains, like our bodies, have an inherited evolutionary design that has scarcely changed for 10,000 years. As respected evolutionary psychology experts Leda Cosmides and John Tooby comment, ‘our modern skulls house a Stone Age mind'. The US biologist Edward O. Wilson sees evolutionary psychology as being a discipline which is based on both sociobiology, which is the study of the biological basis of social behaviour, and psychology, which is the systematic study of human behaviour.

Nigel Nicholson, an organisational psychologist from the London Business School, is a strong supporter of evolutionary psychology and on this subject has published Managing the Human Animal. His book takes the reader on a journey from the Stone Age plains of the savannah to the modern office, and includes a discussion of Darwinism and behavioural psychology, together with a dissection of dysfunctional organisational behaviour. It is an effective approach explaining why people behave as they do, particularly at work. Evolutionary psychology is increasingly being cited in management circles, where managers are trying to understand puzzling aspects of human behaviour and, by doing so, improve the workplace. Nicholson believes that evolutionary psychology can help managers understand what goes wrong in organisational life and what they can do about it.

Nicholson maintains that evolutionary psychology dismisses the long-held assumption that our minds are like blank pages just waiting for culture and experience to write on them and shape our nature. He points out that sophisticated research shows the brain actually houses a store of knowledge when we are born, and now genetic research is establishing there are certain genes that account for abilities, tastes and tendencies. The stored knowledge in the human brain has not changed much since the Stone Age. As Tooby and Cosmides stress, there have not been enough generations for a brain that is well-adapted to our post-industrial life to evolve through natural selection.

The evolutionary psychology version of human nature revolves around some key elements which we have inherited from our hunter-gatherer minds. One key element is emotion. Emotion was originally essential to keep early man alive and safe from predators. Emotion was, and continues to be, our radar, guiding us throughout today's techno-defined business world. Despite this, the business world emphasises rational, not emotional, behaviour, and does not admit the importance of emotion. We still use the emotional part of our minds to make sense of other people's behaviour and to create an impression, so we can often be taken in by appearances. This mental predisposition actually works best in small communities (the tribe), not in much larger environments filled with people we barely know (the modern workplace). Our minds naturally try to re-create our ancestral communities with networks of no more than 150 people, where there are clear hierarchies and leaders. As a consequence, it takes very little to trigger people's innate distrust of others because our safety in antiquity depended on supporting our near family and friends, whom we valued more than other people.

So what advice does Nicholson have for the corporate world? He thinks that by knowing the reasons for people's behaviour it is possible to mould corporate environments into places that have more chance of working efficiently and being pleasant places to work in. Nicholson admits that not everybody in the business world agrees with his belief in the effectiveness of evolutionary psychology in the workplace. One group that resists the theory of evolutionary psychology is young MBA graduates who are just beginning their careers and feel that evolutionary psychology will make their lives at work more difficult. Older and wiser executives point out that they still tend to cling to the idea of a magic formula to bring people into line with corporate strategy. But that is back-to-front thinking, according to Nicholson, who contends that we should be reinventing our business structures, not our fundamental human nature.

At the end of his book, Nicholson gives his forecast of what will and will not change in the business world. He believes that most people will still prefer more traditional forms of work and throughout their lives will continue to aim at lifelong status advancement. He also maintains that the line between work and home will be less defined, but that people will prefer traditional working patterns if working from home leaves them isolated from their work community. He doubts that the high-tech ideas of virtual companies will ever be very successful because people will still want to meet each other face-to-face. Nicholson describes his ideal organisation in the future: it would be decentralised, with small sub-units; the staff would be from diverse backgrounds and be allowed a high degree of self-determination. New endeavours and creativity would replace systems and rationality. Nicholson acknowledges that there is a long way to go in terms of the translation of his ideas of evolutionary psychology into practical propositions, but he is confident more and more people will come round to his way of thinking.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 1
passageNotes.text: 进化论创立者查尔斯・达尔文（Charles Darwin）通常不与现代商业世界关联，但达尔文进化理论是 “进化心理学”（解释人类普遍行为及职场行为的新思潮）的基础。进化心理学核心观点是：人类大脑与身体一样，具有 1 万年未显著变化的遗传进化设计，正如专家莉达・科斯米德斯（Leda Cosmides）和约翰・图比（John Tooby）所言 “现代颅骨中装着石器时代的大脑”。美国生物学家爱德华・O・威尔逊（Edward O. Wilson）认为，进化心理学融合了 “社会生物学（研究社会行为的生物基础）” 与 “心理学（系统研究人类行为）”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 2
passageNotes.text: 伦敦商学院组织心理学家奈杰尔・尼科尔森（Nigel Nicholson）是进化心理学的坚定支持者，著有《管理人类动物》（_Managing the Human Animal_）。该书将读者从石器时代草原带至现代办公室，探讨达尔文主义与行为心理学，剖析组织功能失调行为，有效解释人类（尤其职场）行为动因。进化心理学在管理领域应用日益广泛，管理者借此理解困惑的人类行为以改善职场。尼科尔森认为，进化心理学可帮助管理者识别组织问题并提供解决方案。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 3
passageNotes.text: 尼科尔森指出，进化心理学推翻了 “大脑如白纸，需文化与经验塑造” 的长期假设。前沿研究显示，人类出生时大脑已储存先天知识，基因研究证实特定基因决定能力、偏好与倾向。石器时代以来，人类大脑的先天知识几乎未变，图比和科斯米德斯强调：自然选择尚未产生适应后工业生活的大脑（代际数量不足）。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 4
passageNotes.text: 进化心理学视角下的人类本质包含源于 “采集者大脑” 的核心要素，情绪是其一。情绪最初帮助早期人类躲避天敌、维持生存，如今仍是 “导航工具”，引导人们在科技主导的商业世界决策。但商业世界强调理性而非情绪，忽视情绪重要性 —— 人们仍通过情绪理解他人行为、塑造印象，这种倾向在 “小部落”（熟人社区）中高效，在 “大职场”（陌生人环境）中则易触发先天的不信任（古代安全依赖亲友，重视程度高于他人）。此外，人类大脑本能倾向于构建 “不超过 150 人的祖先式社区”，需要明确层级与领导者。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 5
passageNotes.text: 尼科尔森对企业界的建议是：理解行为动因可将企业环境改造为 “高效且舒适的工作场所”。他承认并非所有商界人士认同其观点 —— 初入职场的年轻 MBA 毕业生认为进化心理学会增加工作难度；资深管理者虽更开放，但仍迷信 “能让员工服从企业战略的神奇公式”。尼科尔森认为这是 “本末倒置”：应改造商业模式，而非改变人类本质。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph 6
passageNotes.text: 尼科尔森在书中预测商界未来变化：多数人仍偏好传统工作形式，终身追求职位晋升；工作与家庭界限虽模糊，但远程办公若导致脱离工作社区，人们仍会选择传统模式；虚拟公司难以成功（人们需要面对面交流）。他理想中的未来组织应 “去中心化、小单元运作、员工背景多元且高度自主、以创新替代制度与理性”。尼科尔森承认，将进化心理学理念转化为实践仍需时日，但坚信会有更多人接受其观点。

items.text:
（1）题目 27：The writer’s purpose in the first paragraph is to（作者在第一段的目的是什么？）
答案：C（explain the theory of evolutionary psychology. 解释进化心理学理论）
解析：定位 Paragraph 1 中 “Darwinian evolutionary theory is the foundation of a new wave of ideas... these ideas have given the title of ‘evolutionary psychology’. Evolutionary psychology revolves around the notion that... Edward O. Wilson sees evolutionary psychology as being a discipline which is based on both sociobiology... and psychology”，第一段核心是 “定义并解释进化心理学的起源与核心观点”，因此选 C。

（2）题目 28：In the third paragraph, which view about evolutionary psychology matches Nicholson’s opinion?（第三段中，哪一观点与尼科尔森对进化心理学的看法一致？）
答案：D（We inherit ideas and characteristics from our ancestors. 我们从祖先那里继承观念与特征）
解析：定位 Paragraph 3 中 “Nicholson maintains that evolutionary psychology dismisses the long-held assumption that our minds are like blank pages... the brain actually houses a store of knowledge when we are born, and now genetic research is establishing there are certain genes that account for abilities, tastes and tendencies”，尼科尔森否定 “白板论”，强调 “先天遗传”，即 “继承祖先的观念与特征”，因此选 D。

（3）题目 29：The writer discusses the key element of emotion in order to（作者讨论 “情绪” 这一核心要素是为了什么？）
答案：B（explain attitudes and actions at work. 解释职场中的态度与行为）
解析：定位 Paragraph 4 中 “Emotion was originally essential to keep early man alive... Emotion was, and continues to be, our radar, guiding us throughout today’s techno-defined business world. We still use the emotional part of our minds to make sense of other people’s behaviour and to create an impression... This mental predisposition actually works best in small communities... not in much larger environments filled with people we barely know (the modern workplace)”，讨论情绪是为了 “解释其对职场态度与行为的影响”，因此选 B。

（4）题目 30：Which of the following does Nicholson predict will happen in the business world?（尼科尔森预测商界将发生以下哪件事？）
答案：D（Social interaction will remain important to workers. 社交互动对员工仍重要）
解析：定位 Paragraph 6 中 “people will prefer traditional working patterns if working from home leaves them isolated from their work community... he doubts that the high-tech ideas of virtual companies will ever be very successful because people will still want to meet each other face-to-face”，明确预测 “人们需要社交互动，远程办公和虚拟公司难以成功”，因此选 D。

（5）题目 31：Which of the following is the most suitable title for Reading Passage 3?（以下哪项最适合作为本文标题？）
答案：B（Understanding the origins of workplace behaviour. 理解职场行为的起源）
解析：全文核心是 “用进化心理学解释职场行为的先天起源”，A “成功公司如何管理变革”、C “现代管理否定达尔文理论”、D “后工业组织需快速进化” 均偏离主旨，因此选 B。

items.text:
（1）题目 32：Nicholson makes a persuasive argument in his book.（尼科尔森在书中的论证具有说服力）
答案：YES（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph 2 中 “It is an effective approach explaining why people behave as they do, particularly at work”，作者评价尼科尔森的方法 “有效”，即 “论证有说服力”，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 YES。

（2）题目 33：Tooby and Cosmides believe natural selection through the generations has prepared us for modern times.（图比和科斯米德斯认为，代际自然选择已让我们适应现代生活）
答案：NO（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph 3 中 “As Tooby and Cosmides stress, there have not been enough generations for a brain that is well-adapted to our post-industrial life to evolve through natural selection”，明确提到 “代际数量不足，自然选择未让大脑适应现代生活”，与题干 “已适应” 描述矛盾，因此判定为 NO。

（3）题目 34：Our reliance on technology causes emotional problems in the workplace.（我们对科技的依赖导致职场中的情绪问题）
答案：NOT GIVEN（未提及）
解析：Paragraph 4 仅提到 “科技主导商业世界，情绪仍是导航工具”，未建立 “科技依赖→情绪问题” 的因果关系，无相关信息，因此判定为 NOT GIVEN。

（4）题目 35：People today are more trusting than they used to be.（如今的人比过去更易信任他人）
答案：NO（错误）
解析：Paragraph 4 提到 “人类先天易触发不信任，古代安全依赖亲友”，与题干“如今的人比过去更易信任他人”相反，因此判定为 NO。

items.text:
（1）题目 36：Nicholson believes that if we know why people act the way they do, we can change \___\___ so employees will work more efficiently.
题目翻译：尼科尔森认为，若了解人们行为的动因，我们可改变_\___\__，使员工工作更高效。
答案：H（business environments，商业环境）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “by knowing the reasons for people’s behaviour it is possible to mould corporate environments into places that have more chance of working efficiently”，“corporate environments” 对应 “business environments”，因此选 H。

（2）题目 37：Nicholson’s ideas are unwelcome to \___\___, but some executives are more open to what evolutionary psychology says.
题目翻译：尼科尔森的观点不受_\___\__欢迎，但部分高管对进化心理学更开放。
答案：B（MBA graduates，MBA 毕业生）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “One group that resists the theory of evolutionary psychology is young MBA graduates who are just beginning their careers”，明确提到 “年轻 MBA 毕业生抵制其观点”，因此选 B。

（3）题目 38：However, these executives still believe that there is a \___\___ that will make employees act according to the company’s practices.
题目翻译：然而，这些高管仍相信存在一种_\___\__，能让员工按公司制度行事。
答案：E（magic formula，神奇公式）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “older and wiser executives... still tend to cling to the idea of a magic formula to bring people into line with corporate strategy”，明确提到 “高管迷信神奇公式”，因此选 E。

（4）题目 39：According to Nicholson, these senior executives are engaging in \___\___.
题目翻译：尼科尔森认为，这些高管陷入了_\___\__。
答案：G（back-to-front thinking，本末倒置的思维）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “But that is back-to-front thinking, according to Nicholson”，明确提到 “高管的想法是本末倒置”，因此选 G。

（5）题目 40：and we should not try to change \___\___ but instead we should change our business structures.
题目翻译：我们不应试图改变_\___\__，而应改变商业模式。
答案：I（human nature，人类本质）
解析：定位 Paragraph 5 中 “who contends that we should be reinventing our business structures, not our fundamental human nature”，明确提到 “不应改变人类本质”，因此选 I。
